body.statement: For every compatible \(\pi\) and every \(n\ge1\), the interval \(\mathrm{CI}_n\) satisfies \[\Pr_{\pi}\bigl([D_1(\pi),U_1(\pi)]\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n\bigr)\ge1-\alpha.\] The guarantee is uniform over boundary and nearly point-identified laws. If endpoint computations use approximation, the same coverage holds when \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{num}}\) is a proven outward bound propagated through the one-Lipschitz backward recursion; a feasible grid value without such a certificate does not qualify.
body.justification: Input-law inversion covers the entire population identified set without relying on differentiability or positive cell probabilities.
body.gap: ChafaiConcordet2009 controls multinomial-law coverage and ImbensManski2004 studies confidence intervals under partial identification, but neither projects an exact region through a nonconvex hazard-spliced endpoint recursion with certified numerical enlargement.
body.consumer: This gives finite-sample reporting for sparse grouped competing-event trials once the exact frontier computation is available.
